Chapter 6: System Design & Implementation

6.1 Unified Modeling Language (UML) Modeling

Object-oriented analysis and structural modeling for AssetDesk are formalized through standard Unified Modeling Language (UML 2.5) diagrams. Figure 6.1 captures functional interactions across three distinct user roles (System Administrator, IT Support Technician, and Standard Employee), depicting secure authentication, operational boundaries, and system event triggers.

Actor Roles & Boundary Scopes: Administrator exercises complete governance (user onboarding, role updates, license reveal, system configuration, audit review, and CSV export). IT Support triages hardware inventory, executes state transitions, and resolves assigned helpdesk tickets. Employee accesses self-service inventory, logs incident tickets, and tracks resolution status.

6.1.1 Structural Class Modeling

Figure 6.2 models domain class attributes, methods, visibility indicators, and persistence associations implemented across Mongoose ODM schemas. Multiplicities capture one-to-many relationships (User to Assets and Tickets) and many-to-many associations (License to Users via subdocument seat allocations).

Domain Entities: Captures complete schema definitions for User, Asset, License, Allocation, Ticket, Comment, and AuditLog. Associations enforce atomic relationship integrity at the database model layer.

6.1.2 Operational Activity Workflows

Activity diagrams specify algorithmic control flows, conditional branch evaluations, and database commit gates across rate-limited session authentication and concurrency-safe hardware asset allocation.

Validates email format, checks rate limit counters, verifies password with salted bcrypt hash, issues signed JWT, and logs audit events.
Verifies caller RBAC permissions, confirms device availability, atomically updates status, commits audit journal entry, and returns updated asset.

6.1.3 Incident Lifecycle & Behavioral State Models

Figure 6.5 diagrams the complete support ticket lifecycle from employee submission to administrative closure. Figures 6.6 and 6.7 formalize finite state machine rules governing ticket progress and hardware inventory lifecycle transitions.

Details sequential code generation, SLA due-date computation, staff triage, threaded comments, mandatory resolution note validation, employee reopening, and closure.
Transitions: OPEN → IN_PROGRESS → RESOLVED → CLOSED. Employees may reopen resolved tickets; closed tickets are immutable.
Transitions: AVAILABLE ↔ ASSIGNED; transition to MAINTENANCE clears assignment; terminal retirement state is RETIRED.

6.2 Database Design & Data Dictionary

The persistence tier is engineered using MongoDB Community Edition with Mongoose ODM schemas. Tables 6.1 through 6.5 specify field types, nullability rules, indices, and foreign key relations ensuring data integrity across all core business collections.

Table 6.1: User Collection Schema Specification (users)
Field Name BSON Type Required Key / Index Functional Role
_idObjectIdYesPKUnique 12-byte document identifier
nameStringYes—User full name (2–100 chars, trimmed)
emailStringYesUnique IndexNormalized lowercase email for authentication
passwordHashStringYes—10-round salted bcrypt hash (omitted in toJSON)
roleStringYesIndexRBAC enum: ADMIN, IT_SUPPORT, EMPLOYEE
departmentStringYes—Institutional department or division name
isActiveBooleanYesIndexAccount state toggle (default: true)
Table 6.2: Asset Collection Schema Specification (assets)
Field Name BSON Type Required Key / Index Functional Role
assetTagStringYesUnique IndexUnique sequential code (AST-YYYY-XXXX)
serialNumberStringYesUnique IndexOEM hardware serial number
name / categoryStringYesIndexDevice label & enum (LAPTOP, DESKTOP, etc.)
statusStringYesCompound IndexLifecycle: AVAILABLE, ASSIGNED, MAINTENANCE, RETIRED
assignedToObjectIdNoFK → UserActive custodian employee user reference
Table 6.3: License & Ticket Schema Specifications (licenses & tickets)
Field Name BSON Type Required Key / Index Functional Role
softwareNameStringYesIndexApplication name and publisher identity
totalSeats / usedSeatsNumberYes—Purchased seat quota and allocated counter
expiryDateDateYesIndex (Asc)Contract renewal date used for expiry alerts
ticketCodeStringYesUnique IndexIncident code format: TCK-YYYY-XXXX
priority / statusStringYesCompound IndexSLA priority (4 tiers) and workflow state (4 states)
dueAt / resolvedAtDateNoIndexDynamic SLA deadline and resolution timestamp

Ticket → User (Author)N : 1Ticket.createdByMandatory reference to author; immutable post-creation
Ticket → User (Tech)N : 1 (0..1)Ticket.assignedToMust reference user with ADMIN or IT_SUPPORT role

6.3 Entity-Relationship (E-R) Diagram & Indexing Strategy

The conceptual data model is expressed in Figure 6.8 as an Entity-Relationship (ER) diagram illustrating Crow’s Foot cardinalities. While MongoDB is a document database, strict referential integrity and high-performance querying are enforced via indexes at the Mongoose ODM layer.

Entity Relationships: User serves as the central hub linked to hardware (Asset), software seats (License), incident requests (Ticket), and audit actions (AuditLog). Counter maintains monotonic counters for atomic code generation.
Table 6.5: Database Indexing Strategy & Performance Optimization
Collection Indexed Field(s) Index Type Query Optimization Rationale
usersemailUnique B-TreeInstantaneous O(1) user login lookup and registration uniqueness
assetsassetTag, serialNumberUnique B-TreePrevents duplicate physical tags and manufacturer hardware serials
assetsstatus, categoryCompound IndexAccelerates inventory pagination; maintains avg latency <7.5ms
licensesexpiryDateAscending IndexOptimizes daily cron scans detecting licenses expiring in 30 days
ticketsstatus, priority, dueAtCompound IndexPowers technician triage queues and real-time SLA overdue highlights
auditlogstimestamp (desc), entityCompound IndexAccelerates compliance audit reviews and date-range CSV reporting

6.5 Implementation: Code Listings & Security Architecture

Core business logic is encapsulated in modular Node.js/Express service controllers. Listings 6.1 through 6.3 show production implementations of authentication middleware, atomic hardware assignment, and ticket state machine validation.

Listing 6.1: JWT Authentication Middleware (server/src/middleware/auth.js)
async function authenticate(req, res, next) { try { const authHeader = req.headers.authorization; if (!authHeader || !authHeader.startsWith("Bearer ")) return next(ApiError.unauthorized("Token required")); const token = authHeader.split(" ")[1]; req.user = jwt.verify(token, config.JWT_SECRET, { algorithms: ["HS256"] }); next(); } catch (err) { return next(ApiError.unauthorized(err.name === "TokenExpiredError" ? "Token expired" : "Invalid token")); } }
Listing 6.2: Atomic Asset Assignment with Concurrency Guard (server/src/controllers/assets.js)
const asset = await Asset.findOneAndUpdate( { _id: req.params.id, status: "AVAILABLE" }, { $set: { status: "ASSIGNED", assignedTo: targetUser._id, assignedAt: new Date() } }, { new: true } ).populate("assignedTo", "name email department"); if (!asset) throw ApiError.badRequest("Asset is not available or concurrently allocated");
Listing 6.3: Ticket State Machine Rules (server/src/services/ticketRules.js)
const VALID_TRANSITIONS = { OPEN: ["IN_PROGRESS"], IN_PROGRESS: ["RESOLVED"], RESOLVED: ["IN_PROGRESS", "CLOSED"], CLOSED: [] }; function canTransition(from, to) { return (VALID_TRANSITIONS[from] || []).includes(to); }
